title: Checks for invalid printf-style format strings.
summary: Conversion specifiers are required for printf-style format strings. These specifiers must contain a % character followed by a conversion type. Ruff takes this rule from Pyflakes and made it stable in v0.0.142.

title: Checks for named placeholders in printf-style format strings without mapping-type values.
summary: When using named placeholders in printf-style format strings, the values must be a map type (such as a dictionary). Otherwise, the expression will raise a TypeError. Ruff takes this rule from Pyflakes and made it stable in v0.0.142.
message_templates: `%`-format string expected mapping but got sequence

title: Checks for uses of mapping-type values in printf-style format strings without named placeholders.
summary: When using mapping-type values (such as dict) in printf-style format strings, the keys must be named. Otherwise, the expression will raise a TypeError. Ruff takes this rule from Pyflakes and made it stable in v0.0.142.
message_templates: `%`-format string expected sequence but got mapping

title: Checks for unused mapping keys in printf-style format strings.
summary: Unused named placeholders in printf-style format strings are unnecessary, and likely indicative of a mistake. They should be removed. Ruff takes this rule from Pyflakes and made it stable in v0.0.142.

title: Checks for named placeholders in printf-style format strings that are not present in the provided mapping.
summary: Named placeholders that lack a corresponding value in the provided mapping will raise a KeyError. Ruff takes this rule from Pyflakes and made it stable in v0.0.142.
message_templates: `%`-format string is missing argument(s) for placeholder(s): {}

title: Checks for printf-style format strings that have mixed positional and named placeholders.
summary: Python does not support mixing positional and named placeholders in printf-style format strings. The use of mixed placeholders will raise a TypeError at runtime. Ruff takes this rule from Pyflakes and made it stable in v0.0.142.
message_templates: `%`-format string has mixed positional and named placeholders

title: Checks for printf-style format strings that have a mismatch between the number of positional placeholders and the number of substitution values.
summary: When a printf-style format string is provided with too many or too few substitution values, it will raise a TypeError at runtime. Ruff takes this rule from Pyflakes and made it stable in v0.0.142.

title: Checks for printf-style format strings that use the * specifier with non-tuple values.
summary: The use of the * specifier with non-tuple values will raise a TypeError at runtime. Ruff takes this rule from Pyflakes and made it stable in v0.0.142.

title: Checks for printf-style format strings with invalid format characters.
summary: In printf-style format strings, the % character is used to indicate placeholders. If a % character is not followed by a valid format character, it will raise a ValueError at runtime. Ruff takes this rule from Pyflakes and made it stable in v0.0.142.

title: Checks for str.format calls with invalid format strings.
summary: Invalid format strings will raise a ValueError. Ruff takes this rule from Pyflakes and made it stable in v0.0.138.

title: Checks for str.format calls with unused keyword arguments.
summary: Unused keyword arguments are redundant, and often indicative of a mistake. They should be removed. Ruff takes this rule from Pyflakes and made it stable in v0.0.139.

title: Checks for str.format calls with unused positional arguments.
summary: Unused positional arguments are redundant, and often indicative of a mistake. They should be removed. Ruff takes this rule from Pyflakes and made it stable in v0.0.139.
message_templates: `.format` call has unused arguments at position(s): {}

title: Checks for str.format calls with placeholders that are missing arguments.
summary: In str.format calls, omitting arguments for placeholders will raise a KeyError at runtime. Ruff takes this rule from Pyflakes and made it stable in v0.0.139.
message_templates: `.format` call is missing argument(s) for placeholder(s): {}

title: Checks for str.format calls that mix automatic and manual numbering.
summary: In str.format calls, mixing automatic and manual numbering will raise a ValueError at runtime. Ruff takes this rule from Pyflakes and made it stable in v0.0.139.
message_templates: `.format` string mixes automatic and manual numbering

title: Checks for f-strings that do not contain any placeholder expressions.
summary: f-strings are a convenient way to format strings, but they are not necessary if there are no placeholder expressions to format. In this case, a regular string should be used instead, as an f-string without placeholders can be confusing for readers, who may expect such a placeholder to be present. Ruff takes this rule from Pyflakes and made it stable in v0.0.18.
